name: Maponus

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Maponus was a Welsh hero or god. A minor Welsh and British divinity, his name is translated as son of the mother or divine youth. He is connected with the goddess Modron, the mother. Several sculptures show him as a naked lad holding a lyre. He may be the same god as Mabon. The Romans equated Maponus with Apollo, which suggests he was linked to the arts. Koch records his cult in Gaul and at Roman military sites in north Britain. A crescent-shaped silver plaque inscribed DEO MAPONO, to the god Maponus, was found at the fort of Vindolanda on Hadrian's Wall. Three dedications to Apollo Maponus were found at Corbridge, and an altar dated to 238-44 at Ribchester. The name survives in the Welsh Mabon fab Modron.
